feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/communications CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant public-sector scope. It reads professionally and shows leadership, but impact is sometimes diluted by dense wording, repeated themes, and limited outcome-focused metrics beyond the website migration.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo from coordinator to director, which supports credibility and career growth.  
- Relevant, modern skill mix: combines strategy, Drupal/CMS delivery, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search in a way that feels current and differentiated.  
- Good evidence of scale: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and enterprise governance responsibilities add weight.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes across roles: include results for email, social, video, campaigns, governance, and analytics improvements, not just responsibilities.  
- Tighten structure and reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidating would improve scannability.  
- Fix style consistency issues: use consistent punctuation in bullets, standardize “organization-wide/organisation-wide” style, and keep serial comma usage consistent. Minor wording tweaks: “10×20-foot” may be clearer as “10 x 20-foot”; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector relevance. However, it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience, and could be sharper by foregrounding scale and outcomes.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and reduce list-like phrasing; replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add 1–2 concrete signals of scale from recent roles (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) to increase impact.
- Use parallel wording and consistent style: “platforms, governance models, and content operations” needs the serial comma for consistency.
- Consider rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads website transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is more specific.
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production” repeats multiple skills sections almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strengths rather than restating broad categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure; avoid mixing “operations,” “systems,” and “communications” unevenly.
- Prioritize the most marketable recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation/integration, and multimedia.
- Consider rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel public-sector communications • Advocacy campaigns and stakeholder communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space is tight, drop either “public-sector” or “stakeholder” wording depending on target role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” closely duplicate the header.
- This section also overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; consider using one for strategic themes and the other for tools/platforms only.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tighten wording, standardize style, and emphasize what is newest or uniquely illustrative rather than restating core responsibilities.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing, and keep each item to one crisp outcome-focused line.
- Standardize verb tense and structure: “Built/Developed/Launched…” + platform/scope + purpose or result.
- Replace vague phrases like “designed for continued campaign growth” with sharper wording such as “built on a reusable modular architecture.”
- Consider: “AI Hybrid Search: Led development of an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign may add the most distinct value because it shows integrated campaign and physical/digital experience design.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a service list. Tighten around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or deliverables to distinguish it from your NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make Drupal/CMS work more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.” Add metrics if possible: number of sites, users, publishers, or turnaround gains.
- Keep the AI search bullet, but make it more distinctive: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content architecture, and user-facing discovery experiences for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance/usability/operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo governance bullets; keep only if tied to a new result.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless linked to a notable launch or scale.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles. Lead with transformation, systems, and measurable scope.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, budget, and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Combine and tighten web impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes explicit where possible: add budget size, team size, reporting improvements, production volume, engagement growth, or efficiency gains from governance/analytics.
- Rephrase weaker bullets to show business value: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring video series.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; either add distinct results here or cut it.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries unless this bullet stresses the studio build and organizational scale-up.

items.title: Associate Communications Director

items.content:

- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Combine newsletter/video bullets and make outcomes clearer: “Owned four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders, and produced a weekly advocacy video series that established video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Recast coordination/process bullets into stronger action language: “Built cross-team editorial planning routines linking communications, advocacy and program staff, improving alignment, publishing consistency and campaign execution.”
- If possible, add metrics: open rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager role and footer project; distinguish this role as scaling/formalizing the series.
- “Improved workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance language; focus here on operational coordination rather than enterprise standards.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems

- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, it should read as a cleaner tools/methods list and avoid broad capability labels already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to specific platforms + methods: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
